heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

GOVERNMENT OF KARANGANYAR REGENCY

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF KARANGANYAR REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Karanganyar Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government Administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Karanganyar.
4. Regional Apparatus is the assistant element to the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies, Regional Technical Institutions, Sub-districts and Urban Villages.
5. Implementation is the form of execution of protection for women and children victims of violence.
6. Protection of women and children victims of violence is every activity aimed at providing a sense of security for victims and protecting their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor and receive protection, whether medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic or psychological protection from all forms of violence and discriminatory actions.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those still in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship, whether physical, sexual, economic, social or psychological to the victim.
10. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT P2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
11. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as KP2A is a Commission that functions to formulate policy programs for the protection of women and children victims of violence with the strategy of Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) and Child Rights Mainstreaming (PHA).
12. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims.
13. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and or other community organizations.
14. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
l5.Population is Indonesian citizens and/or foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

The implementation of protection for victims of violence aims to prevent, protect victims and provide services to women based on gender and the best interests of children that occur in the household and/or public.

CHAPTER III

heading: RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
translated_text:
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 4

Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regional Government and community.

heading: Article 5
translated_text:
Article 5

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain health services and assistance, both psychologically and legally, and to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of the community.

heading: CHAPTER IV
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutional

heading: Article 7
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Handling and Mechanism

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the KP2A framework.
2. KP2A in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, may partner with social community institutions engaged in the protection of women and children.
3. The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must pay attention to religious norms, as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
4. The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to standard operating procedures (SOP) which will be further regulated by Regent's Regulation.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Service Principles

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

The implementation of services for victims is carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discrimination, easily accessible, and with a guarantee of confidentiality.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION

heading: Article 10
Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. Every victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
2. Protection for victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided to every resident of Karanganyar Regency, both those who experience violence in the Karanganyar Regency Region and outside the Karanganyar Regency Region.
3. Protection for victims of violence in addition to being provided to residents of Karanganyar Regency as referred to in paragraph (2), also applies to non-residents of Karanganyar Regency that occurs in the Karanganyar Regency Region.

heading: Article 12
CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 13

1. The Regional Government in organizing protection for victims of violence, may involve community participation.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community institutions.

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. Social community institutions that participate in the organization of protection for victims of violence as referred to in Article 13 paragraph (2) are provided guidance by the Regional Government through Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

SOURCES OF FUNDS

Article 15

1. The source of funds for organizing protection for victims of violence comes from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
2. In addition to the source of funds as referred to in paragraph (1), it may also come from other lawful sources.
3. The source of funds for organization from other lawful sources as referred to in paragraph (2) is supervised in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 16

Institutions that violate service principles may be subject to administrative sanctions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 17

Other matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation shall be further regulated by the Regent.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Karanganyar Regency.

heading: CONCERNING
translated_text:
CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The Government has an obligation to provide a sense of security and freedom for every member of its society from all forms of violence in the form of threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, as mandated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, which protects the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, consequently the Government of Indonesia must comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XV of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as outlined in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in community, national and state life.

From the series of policy provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at the national and regional levels.

heading: II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE
translated_text:
II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

Sufficiently clear.

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Letter b
Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women; Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Letter c
Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

Letter d
Sufficiently clear.

heading: Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

What is meant by "gender-based violence" is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.

heading: Article 4:
translated_text:
Article 4:

What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions both government and non-government. Receiving information about the whereabouts of complaint centers, PPT and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and development of case handling.

What is meant by "integrated services" are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by "continuous handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including the restoration of their good name.

heading: Article 5
translated_text:
Article 5

What is meant by "receiving psychological and legal assistance" is receiving psychological and legal assistance at every level of examination and during the judicial process.
